set.body:
Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-18-best-recall-to-video-mapper.md §3 Phase 0 item 6.

On 2026-09-18 the eight FilmFestival films plus the cartoon were copied from Trillium (/project/rrg-brad/dsets/filmfestival/stimuli and /scratch/brad/ff_stim/transcripts) into data/filmfestival/media (1.05 GB, ignored). SHA256SUMS.local there matches the remote for all 53 files. Clips match scan durations to the second except bus_stop (406 s vs 414 s; the source is short). docs/data/filmfestival/README.md:40-41 says FILMS.md names commercial works and is not for Git admission, so titles and source URLs stay in the ignored root.

Scope:
A committed, content-free record plus corrections in the ignored root.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A committed manifest under docs/data/filmfestival/ lists every file under data/filmfestival/media by relative path (cover names only), SHA-256 and size, and for videos container, codec and duration; it matches SHA256SUMS.local line for line.
2. Per film, the committed manifest records trim_start, clip duration and scan duration by cover name; bus_stop's 8 s shortfall is explicit. Source URLs and real titles are not committed.
3. The two commercial excerpts' boundaries are recorded in the committed manifest as annotation segment numbers and run-relative times (content-free); data/filmfestival/FILMS.md (ignored) is corrected to say the_prisoner is mid-episode (cafe to shop exit), and a note on this bead records that correction because it is not visible in Git.
4. The Trillium upstream paths are recorded in the committed manifest.
5. `git check-ignore data/filmfestival/media/clips/bus_stop.mp4` succeeds; no media, frames, transcripts or URLs are committed.
6. docs/data/filmfestival/source-manifest.json keeps admissionStatus.state = proposed unless the owner decides otherwise, and README states the media are staged locally at data/filmfestival/media.

Gate: fresh-context cold review of the committed text; the commit body states what changed and
what it does not establish.

Size: S.
set.title: Phase 0: record the FilmFestival media -- a content-free hash manifest and corrected excerpt boundaries
